Hart's method ("Sphere tracing: a geometric method for the antialiased ray tracing of implicit surfaces", The Visual Computer, 1996): the scene says how far is surely empty, so step that far and ask again. Stops on a surface, past 20, or after 120 steps. A loop on the GPU, since the call to itself is its last step.

The normal, the direction the surface faces, is the gradient of the scene: how fast scene changes along x, along y and along z, as one Vec. gradient reads it off scene itself (for the GPU, before the shader is compiled), so it is exact and follows any edit to scene, instead of being estimated by sampling nearby points (computing normals from the distance's gradient is standard practice; differentiating the program before compiling it for the GPU is what Enzyme does).
t4pma75h0imolv3puct9l0h2hb: What the camera sees through the pixel at (x, y): follow a ray from the camera through it and shade what it hits, fading into the sky with distance; or show the sky.
t353g46bonarkbro9sbp03amv0: The colour of the pixel at (x, y): what trace sees, or magenta when it has no answer (a division by 0 in shadow), so a pixel that hasn't shows. march and shadow count their steps in an Int, and a count that goes up by 1 to a bound is sure to stop, so the checker knows they end. with fuel stays only because the plain scalar profile takes first in that shape alone; it never runs out. A budget like this is an old idea: gas in Ethereum, fuel in Wasmtime.
program:
Adapted: march is sphere tracing, John C. Hart's method ("Sphere tracing: a geometric method for the antialiased ray tracing of implicit surfaces", The Visual Computer, 1996).
Adapted: the ring's distance, the smooth minimum and the soft shadow are Inigo Quilez's formulas: https://iquilezles.org/articles/distfunctions/ https://iquilezles.org/articles/smin/ https://iquilezles.org/articles/rmshadows/
Our own: the scene (a drop in a ring over a checker floor), and normals read off the scene by gradient before the shader is compiled.
Prior art: differentiating a program before compiling it for the GPU is what Enzyme does (Moses and Churavy, NeurIPS 2020).
Influence: the fuel budget is an old idea: gas in Ethereum, fuel in Wasmtime.
mrbdfq8n6tv0re4tjh27a0mtls: Pga's sixteen basis elements, each 1 in its own place, in clifford table's order: e₀ is the fourth vector, so e₂₃₀ is e₂e₃e₀.
6h9sro4imrsg7cdckjr5eojs6p: Projective geometric algebra (PGA), an algebra for 3D geometry where points, planes and motions are one kind of value, Cl(3, 0, 1): three vectors that square to 1 and e₀, which squares to 0. One kind of value, a motor, both turns and moves, and two motors make one by their product. This is Charles Gunn's PGA, as in Gunn and De Keninck's "Geometric Algebra for Computer Graphics" (SIGGRAPH 2019).
4jtfvdemc9a3nnl0aq49252219: The point v in projective geometric algebra: e₁₂₃ − x e₂₃₀ + y e₁₃₀ − z e₁₂₀, as Gunn and De Keninck write a point.
qlvn1422c30l307hkaoefh31gj: Where the point m is, back as a Vec. A motor keeps a point's e₁₂₃ at 1, so its other three parts are x, y and z.
pfah14n3fmo23krgnonufsjntp: How the ring sits at this time, as one motor: tilted about the x axis by up to 0.3 radians (the rotor cos ½θ − sin ½θ e₂₃), then lifted by up to 0.12 (the translator 1 + ½d e₂₀). Their product turns and moves at once.
5a0r203toui9h5da8thvaevq3r: How far p is from the ring where halo motor puts it. Instead of moving the ring, move p the other way, by the motor's reverse M̃ (M̃ p M), and ask how far it is from the ring at rest. Moving the point instead of the shape is the usual way with distance functions.
